transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Thompson. It is good to see you again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hello doctor. I was just wondering about those tests. My daughter said you wanted to talk.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I wanted to sit down with you to discuss your recent lab results and some information we gave you last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it about that condition? The one you mentioned? I've been quite worried about it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are worried, and I want to start by saying I am very sorry. Our team made a mistake with your records.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, things didn't go quite right with the paperwork. There was some confusion in the scheduling system regarding the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Did I have the sickness or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the files. It seems like the information we discussed last time wasn't actually yours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't follow. Was the report wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mix-up in the system. Some things got switched around.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, so you told me I was ill, but now you are saying the system had an issue? Am I okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for the stress this has caused you. I know it is frightening to be told you have a medical condition.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was very frightening. I couldn't sleep for three days. I told my son I might be leaving soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like this has been a very heavy burden for you and your family to carry this week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It has. But I still don't know what happened. Why did this happen to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the scheduling system just didn't process the data correctly. It was a systemic error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But who did the error? Did the nurse do it? Did you do it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team and I are responsible for ensuring the right results go to the right patient, and we failed to do that in this case. I apologize deeply for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, do I have the condition or not? Please, just tell me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Based on what we know now, you do not have the condition we discussed last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't have it? I'm healthy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I cannot say you are perfectly healthy, but you definitely do not have that specific illness.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh thank god. Oh, thank goodness. I felt like the world was ending.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am glad to hear you feel relieved. I know it is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did you tell me I had it if you weren't sure?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the labels on the lab results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't quite get it. Were the papers swapped?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a bit of a glitch in how the names were listed in the computer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds like a very big mistake for a hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I agree. It is not how we want to provide care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Do I have to do more tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is what we are going to do. I am going to personally re-order all of your blood work today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Today? Do I have to stay here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you can stay home. I will have the nurse come and draw your blood in the next twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Twenty minutes. Okay. And when will I know the real answer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you personally on Thursday afternoon with the final results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will call me? Not my daughter?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you directly on your home phone, and I will also call your daughter so you both have the news at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That would be better. I don't like waiting for the mail.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Your only job right now is to wait for the nurse to come in and then head home to relax.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I can do that. I just wish this hadn't happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand. We are going to make sure we get the correct answers this time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you make sure the other person gets their news too?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are working on correcting the records for everyone involved right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope they are okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you for your kindness, Mr. Thompson.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are welcome, doctor. I'll wait for the nurse.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be back in a moment to make sure the nurse has arrived.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a steady pace during distress, and never interrupts.

E.justification: The resident relies entirely on platitudes and vague hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'confusion in the scheduling system', 'mix-up') without explicitly naming the error (e.g., 'we gave you another patient's results').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize deeply') and explicitly accepts responsibility for the team's failure.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('worried', 'frightening', 'heavy burden') and references the patient's specific experience of not sleeping and talking to his son.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps (re-ordering blood work), timelines (next 20 minutes, Thursday afternoon), the patient's role (wait for nurse, head home), and addresses prevention (correcting records for everyone).
